target: Der Film, den wir gestern gesehen haben, war fantastisch.
english: The film we saw yesterday was fantastic.
tip: 'War/waren' (was/were) is the Präteritum of 'sein' – one of the few verbs where Präteritum is preferred over Perfekt in speech.

target: Ihr könnt das Fahrrad gerne ausleihen.
english: You (plural) are welcome to borrow the bicycle.
tip: Modal verbs take position 2 and push the main verb to infinitive at the end: 'Ich kann/muss/will/soll/darf ... [infinitive]'.

target: Sie will endlich ihren Führerschein machen.
english: She finally wants to get her driver's license.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'machen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Die Schneiderin will das Brautkleid anpassen.
english: The seamstress wants to alter the wedding dress.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'anpassen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Die Therapeutin will die Traumata aufarbeiten.
english: The therapist wants to work through the traumas.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'aufarbeiten' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er erklärt den Schülern die komplizierten Formeln.
english: He explains the complicated formulas to the students.
tip: Adjective 'komplizierten' – its ending depends on the article type, case, and noun gender. After definite articles, usually -e or -en.

target: Wir widmen dieses Lied unseren verstorbenen Großeltern.
english: We dedicate this song to our deceased grandparents.
tip: Dative: 'widmen' takes dative – 'unseren verstorbenen Großeltern'.

target: Ich rate dir, einen warmen Mantel mitzunehmen.
english: I advise you to take a warm coat.
tip: Dative: 'raten' takes dative – 'dir' (dative of 'du').

target: Das Spielzeug fehlt dem kleinen Mädchen sehr.
english: The little girl misses the toy very much.
tip: Dative: 'fehlen' takes dative – 'dem kleinen Mädchen'.

target: Die Länge des Kurses beträgt sechs Wochen.
english: The length of the course is six weeks.
tip: 'des Kurses' – genitive case showing possession. Masculine/neuter nouns add -s or -es.

target: Darf ich Ihnen eine Tasse Tee anbieten?
english: May I offer you a cup of tea?
tip: 'Dürfen' in questions expresses polite requests for permission.

target: Ich will nächstes Jahr nach Japan reisen.
english: I want to travel to Japan next year.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'reisen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er darf nach dem Essen draußen spielen.
english: He is allowed to play outside after eating.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'spielen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich darf heute früher nach Hause gehen.
english: I am allowed to go home earlier today.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'gehen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Sie putzt die ganze Wohnung vor dem Besuch.
english: She cleans the whole apartment before the visit.
tip: Verbs with stem in -tz: putzen → du putzt (just -t, no extra s).

target: Darf ich Ihnen schon etwas zu trinken bringen?
english: May I bring you something to drink already?
tip: 'Darf' (modal) pushes 'bringen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Sie will nach dem Studium im Ausland arbeiten.
english: She wants to work abroad after her studies.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'arbeiten' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Zugegebenermaßen war mein erster Versuch nicht besonders gelungen.
english: Admittedly my first attempt was not particularly successful.
tip: 'Zugegebenerma' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Du darfst dir aus dem Regal ein Buch aussuchen.
english: You may choose a book from the shelf.
tip: 'darfst' (modal) pushes 'aussuchen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Wir können die Wanderung bei diesem Nebel nicht fortsetzen.
english: We cannot continue the hike in this fog.
tip: 'können' (modal) pushes 'fortsetzen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Das war der kälteste Winter seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen.
english: That was the coldest winter since records began.
tip: 'Aufzeichnungen' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Ich glaube dem Verkäufer kein einziges Wort.
english: I don't believe the salesman one bit.
tip: Dative: 'glauben' takes dative for the person – 'dem Verkäufer'.

target: Das Alter des Gebäudes sieht man sofort.
english: You can see the age of the building immediately.
tip: After 'mit' (with), always use dative: 'mit dem Auto' (by car), 'mit meiner Freundin' (with my girlfriend).

target: Sie muss ihre Doktorarbeit bis September fertigstellen.
english: She has to finish her doctoral thesis by September.
tip: 'muss' (modal) pushes 'fertigstellen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Wir dürfen im Naturschutzgebiet keine Pflanzen pflücken.
english: We may not pick plants in the nature reserve.
tip: 'Dürfen' with 'nicht' expresses prohibition – 'not allowed to'.

target: Er dient dem Unternehmen seit über zwanzig Jahren.
english: He has served the company for over twenty years.
tip: Dative: 'dienen' takes dative – 'dem Unternehmen'.

target: Die Bewerbungen werden von der Personalabteilung sorgfältig geprüft.
english: The applications are carefully reviewed by the HR department.
tip: 'von' + dative marks the agent in passive sentences.

target: Wir müssen unsere Reisepässe vor dem Flug kontrollieren.
english: We have to check our passports before the flight.
tip: 'müssen' (modal) pushes 'kontrollieren' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er will im nächsten Semester ein Auslandspraktikum machen.
english: He wants to do an internship abroad next semester.
tip: 'Auslandspraktikum' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Abgesehen von dem Wetter war unser Campingurlaub wunderbar.
english: Apart from the weather, our camping holiday was wonderful.
tip: 'Campingurlaub' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Das Bild hängt an der Wand über dem Sofa.
english: The picture hangs on the wall above the sofa.
tip: 'An' + dative: location – 'an der Wand' (position).

target: Der Taucher erforschte das gesunkene Schiff auf dem Meeresgrund.
english: The diver explored the sunken ship on the seabed.
tip: Adjective 'gesunkene' – its ending depends on the article type, case, and noun gender. After definite articles, usually -e or -en.

target: Sie kann den Sachverhalt besser als jeder andere erklären.
english: She can explain the matter better than anyone else.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'ren' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich kann dieses Wochenende leider nicht zum Geburtstag kommen.
english: Unfortunately I cannot come to the birthday this weekend.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'kommen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Sie kann besonders gut mit Zahlen und Statistiken umgehen.
english: She is particularly good at handling numbers and statistics.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'umgehen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er will seine Großeltern unbedingt noch vor Weihnachten besuchen.
english: He absolutely wants to visit his grandparents before Christmas.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'besuchen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Wir fahren nicht mit dem Zug, sondern mit dem Auto.
english: We are not going by train but by car.
tip: 'Nicht ... sondern' means 'not ... but rather' – corrective negation.

target: Ich soll dir Grüße von meiner Schwester ausrichten.
english: I am supposed to pass on greetings from my sister.
tip: 'Sollen' here conveys a message from someone else – 'I was told to'.

target: Sie muss die Abschlusspräsentation nächste Woche allein halten.
english: She has to give the final presentation alone next week.
tip: 'muss' (modal) pushes 'halten' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich will mein Spanisch in den nächsten Monaten verbessern.
english: I want to improve my Spanish in the coming months.
tip: 'will' (modal) pushes 'verbessern' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du kannst den Kuchen ruhig mit den Fingern essen.
english: You can eat the cake with your fingers, it's fine.
tip: 'kannst' (modal) pushes 'essen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Sie darf nach zweiundzwanzig Uhr die Waschmaschine nicht benutzen.
english: She may not use the washing machine after 10 p.m.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'benutzen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Du musst den Mietvertrag vor dem Einzug sorgfältig durchlesen.
english: You have to read the lease carefully before moving in.
tip: 'musst' (modal) pushes 'durchlesen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Er bietet seinen Platz im Bus älteren Leuten an.
english: He offers his seat on the bus to older people.
tip: Offering your seat to the elderly is considered a sign of good manners in Germany.

target: Trotz des regnerischen Wetters hatten wir einen wunderbaren gemeinsamen Ausflug.
english: Despite the rainy weather, we had a wonderful shared outing.
tip: 'Hatte' is Präteritum of 'haben' – like 'war', commonly used in speech instead of the Perfekt form.

target: Ich darf morgen ausnahmsweise von zu Hause arbeiten.
english: I am allowed to work from home tomorrow as an exception.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'arbeiten' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Mein alter Schulweg war doppelt so lang wie der meiner Kinder.
english: My old school route was twice as long as my children's.
tip: Adjective 'meiner' – its ending depends on the article type, case, and noun gender. After definite articles, usually -e or -en.

target: Es wäre an der Zeit, dass wir uns ernsthaft mit dem Thema befassen.
english: It would be about time that we engage seriously with the topic.
tip: 'Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren' = standard formal salutation.

target: Der Familienausflug zum Freizeitpark war ein voller Erfolg für alle.
english: The family trip to the amusement park was a complete success for everyone.
tip: 'Familienausflug' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Sie hätte das Konzert gern besucht, aber die Karten waren ausverkauft.
english: She would have liked to attend the concert, but the tickets were sold out.
tip: 'hätte' – konjunktiv II of haben (hat), softening this into a hypothetical or polite expression.

target: Sie kann sehr schnell tippen.
english: She can type very fast.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'tippen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Der Klempner kann die Rohrleitung reparieren.
english: The plumber can repair the pipeline.
tip: 'kann' (modal) pushes 'reparieren' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ein kalter Wind weht von Norden.
english: A cold wind blows from the north.
tip: After 'ein': adj. takes '-er' (nom. masculine).

target: Ausnahmsweise erlaubt der Chef heute früher Feierabend.
english: As an exception, the boss is letting them finish early today.
tip: 'Ausnahmsweise' – compound noun. The last component determines gender; earlier components modify meaning.

target: Wir müssen am Alexanderplatz in die U-Bahn umsteigen.
english: We have to transfer to the subway at Alexanderplatz.
tip: 'Umsteigen' – 'to transfer/change' – very common in German public transport.

target: Ich muss meine Eltern am Wochenende unbedingt besuchen.
english: I absolutely have to visit my parents on the weekend.
tip: 'muss' (modal) pushes 'besuchen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Sie sagte, sie wolle nächstes Jahr nach Kanada auswandern.
english: She said she wanted to emigrate to Canada next year.
tip: 'habe' + Partizip II = Konj. I perfect in reported speech.

target: Er darf erst nach der Probezeit Urlaub nehmen.
english: He is only allowed to take vacation after the probation period.
tip: 'darf' (modal) pushes 'nehmen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.

target: Ich bin heute noch müder als gestern nach dem Training.
english: I am even more tired today than yesterday after the training.
tip: 'müder als' – comparative. Some adjectives also umlaut: groß→größer, alt→älter, lang→länger, jung→jünger.

target: Wir müssen die Steuererklärung bis Ende Mai einreichen.
english: We have to submit the tax return by the end of May.
tip: 'müssen' (modal) pushes 'einreichen' to the infinitive at the sentence end – the modal verb frame is fundamental to German.
